feedback.problem: Express $\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{2}{sin}^{2}⁡{36}^{∘}$ as a single trigonometric ratio.
feedback.worked_solution:
Our expression can be factored as follows:

$$
\frac{1}{4}(1-2{sin}^{2}⁡{36}^{∘})
$$

Now, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x={36}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}1-2{sin}^{2}⁡{36}^{∘} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot {36}^{∘})=\operatorname{cos}⁡{72}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\frac{1}{4}(1-2{sin}^{2}⁡{36}^{∘})=\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡{72}^{∘}.
$$
